checks.finding: Met object 10159, accession 33.61, George Caleb Bingham, 1845, oil on canvas 73.7 × 92.7 cm. The American Art-Union changed the artist's original historically racialized father-son title to Fur Traders Descending the Missouri.

Met official introduction calls the unusually calm luminous frontier an idealization aimed at eastern viewers. Mohawk scholar Scott Manning Stevens contextualizes the original father-son reference with historical marriages between French traders and Indigenous women that created trade networks and duties of reciprocity, not a demonstrated genealogy for any particular living model.
